episode: Master Bathroom Remodel, The Angle House
assessment: A strong reveal tour episode. The before is easy to read on a phone, a bathroom full of angled walls, and the finished master carries ten named upgrades that each land in a couple of seconds. The main bath and the closet are good but would split the Short, so they stay in the long video. The cost tease at 1:45 to 2:05 is fenced off, Mike handles cost with his own end slides.

project_context.summary: Master suite and main bath remodel on the Angle House, named by the homeowner's son for all its angled walls. The walls moved and squared off, the jetted tub became a freestanding tub with a hand made bath table, the angled shower became a big rectangle with a tiled linear drain and a full width LED niche, and the vanity went to custom walnut with a drawer under each sink. The floor is 48 by 48 tile and heated.
project_context.segment_choice: One Short, a reveal tour. It opens on the angled shower before so the viewer sees why the house got its name, one progress beat for the turn, then the finished master one upgrade at a time.
notes: Every beat after the turn plays over finished house footage.
Nothing in the Short shows demo, workers, or price.

shorts.full_vo: I built my client a custom bath table for her phone, candle, and drink. This master bath was full of angles, and now there isn't a single one left. So we moved the walls and squared everything off. The makeup desk has a lighted mirror and LED lighting underneath. The vanity is all custom walnut, and the gold fixtures actually match. 48 inch floor tiles mean way fewer grout lines. The freestanding tub has its own filler with a hand spray. The huge shower has a linear drain with tile right in it. The niche runs the full width, lit with LEDs. There's a bidet toilet, with a cabinet right above it. Under each sink, the dead panel became one more drawer. And the whole floor is heated, with a programmable thermostat.
shorts.voice_direction: Warm and unhurried, a contractor walking a friend through the finished room. Plain delivery, no announcer push. Let the features do the work.
